goal: Make learner-facing Academy content English-only and revise DB-01 into a clearly taught, learner-guided lesson.

in_scope: Set the project language policy in PROJECT_SPEC.md to English for all learner-facing content.
Set the Database module README and content guidelines to English-only learner-facing prose.
Revise only Database lesson DB-01 into an English lesson with a clear teaching sequence, causal explanations, progressive worked example, trade-offs, exercise, solution, and knowledge checks.
Audit DB-02 through DB-08 for learner-facing language; leave them unchanged if already English.
Record the language and teaching-quality audit and required validation results in this task run directory.
out_of_scope: Rewriting lessons DB-02 through DB-08 or content in another module unless the audit finds learner-facing non-English prose.
Translating historical workflow snapshots, prior reviews, prior task logs, or internal task records.
Adding new vendor-specific behavior or technical claims without source review.
Approving, merging, or publishing any learner-facing content.

constraints: All current and future learner-facing course content must be written entirely in English; source titles and quotations retain their original language.
Preserve DB-01 technical scope, claim-level citations, and PostgreSQL 18 examples; do not claim that SQL was executed.
Use original explanations, worked examples, diagrams, exercises, questions, and answers; do not translate the System Design Primer paragraph by paragraph.
Keep DB-01 status as draft and estimated learner time provisional.
Make the lesson teach before it assesses: introduce a motivating problem, explain each modeling decision step by step, and show how requirements lead to the final schema before formal checks.

definition_of_done.text: The project specification, Database README, and Database content guidelines clearly require English-only learner-facing content.

DB-01 is fully English and follows a teach-first sequence with a motivating problem, progressive mechanism explanation, worked order-domain example, causal trade-offs and failure modes, an outcome-aligned exercise with solution or rubric, and 5–8 knowledge checks with explanations.

The task report identifies DB-01 as the language exception and confirms whether DB-02 through DB-08 are already English; historical internal workflow artifacts are explicitly out of the learner-facing language scope.
The content validator, unit test suite, and task-state validator are run and reported accurately, with structural validation distinguished from factual, legal, and pedagogical approval.
All declared outputs are committed and task automation reaches automation_complete without inferring human approval or publication.

acceptance_criteria.text: Only PROJECT_SPEC.md, Database README, Database content guidelines, DB-01, and task-specific run artifacts change; DB-02 through DB-08 remain untouched if the audit confirms English.

A learner can follow a coherent path from requirements and access patterns to entities, relationships, constraints, schema, normalization, and conditional denormalization; the explanatory material precedes the end-of-lesson knowledge check.
Every DB-01 learning outcome maps to at least one assessment, and each knowledge check can be answered from concepts taught in the lesson.
Existing product/version claims retain nearby direct references and applicable version scope; no new unsupported factual claim is introduced.
The canonical DB-01 lesson remains status: draft and no approval or publication state is added.
All required structural and repository validation commands are recorded with exact outcomes, including host-dependent skips.
